Sara K: Hey team — noticed a sharp p99 spike for /v1/generate on redwood-large-1 around 09:10 UTC. Baseline p99 was ~320ms, now hitting ~900–1.1s. Happened during a 100rps load test. Sample request id: r-0a9f3c2b. Can someone triage?

Miguel R: Thanks Sara. Can you drop the full request id(s) and one curl that reproduces the call? Also need concurrency and token counts used during the test (prompt tokens + max_tokens).

Sara K: Request IDs I have: r-0a9f3c2b, r-0a9f3d44, r-0a9f3f11. Test details: concurrency=24 clients, each sending 2 req/s, prompt ~420 tokens, max_tokens=128. Here's a minimal curl we used (sanitized key):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":128}'
```

Miguel R: Perfect. Can you also grab the debug bundle (support debug tool) for one of the request ids? e.g. `support debug-bundle r-0a9f3c2b --include-logs --include-profiling` — that provides runtime logs + kernel timings. If you can't run that, attach the `proxy.log` and `runtime.log` snippets around the request id.

Sara K: Pasted runtime snippet from runtime.log (cut):

```
[2026-04-23T09:10:18Z] req=r-0a9f3c2b model=redwood-large-1 seq=1 latency=1123ms kvcache_miss=true batch_size=16 kernel_select=opt_v2
[2026-04-23T09:10:18Z] req=r-0a9f3c2b stage=token_gen token=256 step_latency=48ms
[2026-04-23T09:10:18Z] req=r-0a9f3c2b error="batch_overflow" queued=3
```

Miguel R: Interesting, batch_overflow + kvcache_miss. That points at batching policy hitting transient overload. Two quick asks: (1) reproduce with a single-client curl loop at concurrency 1 but with same prompt/token sizes to see per-request latency; (2) run a controlled repro with `--concurrency 16` and `--rps 2` for 5 minutes so eng-runtime can attach profiler. I'll run the same locally with the curl you provided.

eng-infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-091: "p99 regression redwood-large-1 during load test". Assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

Dinesh P: I pulled the debug snippet. Can you also include model config: quantization profile (int8/4), kernel flags, and whether dedicated nodes were used? If this was on Dedicated, include pool id. If Hosted, include region.

Sara K: Hosted in us-west-2, default quantization was int8. No dedicated pools. Kernel flags: default. Pool id: N/A.

Olivia S: Billing/contact note — customer not impacted for prod, this was internal load test. No billing breaks reported.

Miguel R: For the repro pack please include: 1) a folder with the 10 prompt variants you used (exact strings), 2) one curl reproducer (as above), 3) a small script that fires at desired concurrency (we use a node/python gist), 4) the debug bundle for r-0a9f3c2b, 5) exact load test timeline (start/end, rps ramp). Zip it and upload to the incident ticket.

Sara K: Uploading repro pack to INC-2026-091 now (link pasted).

Dinesh P: I'll run the repro with `--concurrency 16 --rps 32` and attach kernel traces. If we see batch_overflow repeatedly, plan is to temporarily loosen batching threshold or add small burst capacity to observe effect.

Jess (oncall): I'll join a quick sync at 10:30 UTC to go over findings. If eng-runtime validates regression, we'll schedule a canary rollback to previous kernel profile. :thumbsup:

Miguel R: One more small tip — if you can reproduce single-client but still see p99 high, include `X-Debug-Mode: kernel-timings` header in the curl so we can capture per-kernel timings in the response metadata.

Sara K: Will add that header and re-run. Thanks all — attaching updated logs to the incident.

Olivia S: Noted — closing customer-facing alert. We'll update internal docs with repro steps once root cause confirmed.
